ChangeSet.Change: Update the Patchhelper to patch list of guid, string or something else.
Update the Patchhelper to be able to patch a list of tuples when configured correctly.
Fix issue allowing to query all organizations when no organization id is set in the request context.
Update to .net 7.
Add scoped services for hangfire
Switch open-telemetry from beta-libraries to stable libraries
Add generic parameter to scoped jobs.
Fixes a bug where Update and Delete using Data.ITransactions do not successfully add the commands to the data transaction in MongoRepositoryBase.
Add Organization settings as optional configuration for each microservice to organization needs.
Add group organization support to settings with groupKey, groupDisplayKey, and groupDisplayName properties for better UI organization and management.
Update OrganizationSettingResult classes to include group information in API responses for frontend organization capabilities.

Add the Ox schema: every service publishes GET /schema, an organisation-independent document describing its queryable entities, their types, keys, relationships and REST operations, with a content-derived revision and ETag. The wire contract, the configuration and the upgrade notes are in OX_SCHEMA.md.

GET /schema is anonymous by default, the same posture as /ModelDefinition, because build tooling and client generators fetch it without credentials. It discloses the persisted shape of every entity (property names and kinds, storage names, enum members, keys, references, routes) and no CLR namespace, no data and nothing about an organisation. A host that does not want that sets OxSchema:RequireAuthorization to true; GET /schema then requires an authenticated caller like GET /schema/addons does.

Serve /ModelDefinition from memory. The document is built once at startup from the same controller list and nothing writes ModelDefinition/ModelDefinition.json any more; the endpoint now answers GET only, and a controller the generator cannot describe is left out instead of replacing the whole document. The per-organisation addon merge of the previous controller is removed: it never applied to the generated document, which is a JSON array the merge could not read, so the served content does not change for any caller. An organisation's addon keys are published by GET /schema/addons.
ModelDefinitionController is sealed, derives from OxSController and takes the OxSchemaRegistry alone.
Add Bootstrap.ConfigureOxSchema so a host can declare the ids an entity retired when it was renamed; they are published as aliases of the entity.
Mark ModelDefinitionBuilder.AddControllerDefinitions obsolete; the registry replaces it and Bootstrap no longer calls it.

The schema is built while the host starts. In the Development and Local environments and under continuous integration (the CI or the TF_BUILD environment variable) an ambiguous document stops the start; every other host logs the findings and serves the document with its diagnostics. A build that throws never stops such a host either: it is logged as critical, /schema serves a document without types that carries the entity-scan-failed diagnostic, and every other route is unaffected.

Bootstrap calls ConfigureModelDefinitions and GetOxQLTypeAssemblies during ConfigureServices. The schema build looks up the MongoDB serializer of every entity and every type reachable from one when the host starts, which freezes their class maps: register class maps and serializers in RegisterServices, not in a static constructor, a hosted service or on first use.

Move to OxQL 2 (OxQL.AspNetCore, OxQL.Core, OxQL.Mongo and OxQL.Studio 2.x, and the new OxQL.Model). The query engine binds against the entity model the schema is built from, and takes every option from the host's OxQL configuration section (limits, OxQL:Compat:Enabled, OxQL:Explain:Enabled, OxQL:Cursor:SigningKey, which falls back to Auth:Token). A host without the section keeps the previous page sizes (MaxPageSize 500, DefaultPageSize 100). A service that references an OxQL package itself has to move to the same version.

Remove OxQLOrganizationFilter. Bootstrap registers OxQLScopeProvider through AddOxQLScope instead, and the engine applies the organisation at every entry into an entity and refuses a request without one. A service that registered the filter itself no longer compiles; delete the registration.

Add POST internal/oxql/batch (internal api key, hidden from the API explorer) and the RemoteQueryClient, through which the engine resolves references into entities another service owns. The calling service needs InternalHosts:{service} and, for an owner that does not answer on v1, the new InternalApiVersions:{service} key; without it the owner appears unreachable.

Add addon definitions: the AddonDefinition controller (GET {entity}, GET by-id/{id}, POST, PUT {id}, DELETE {id}) stores an organisation's typed addon keys in the service's collection model_definition.addon_definition.{service}, the engine filters and sorts on them, and GET /schema/addons publishes them in the schema's descriptor format.

The OpenAPI document of every service changes: GET /OxQL/types is removed (GET /schema replaces it), POST /OxQL/batch is added, the request and result schemas of the OxQL routes are those of contract 2, and the five AddonDefinition operations are added. Generated API clients change on their next regeneration. Callers written against contract 1 keep working at runtime through the engine's compatibility binder while OxQL:Compat:Enabled is on, which is the default.
OxQL engine faults carry their message in the Development and local environments only.

AuthorizeInternalApiKey compares the key in constant time, refuses every call when the configured Auth:InternalApiKey is blank, and answers a controller that does not derive from OxSInternalController with 400 without running the action.

The query engine's startup check of the model's remote references fails fast on the same continuous-integration value as the schema build: the CI or the TF_BUILD environment variable, or what a host states through ConfigureOxSchema. A host is strict in both checks or in neither.

Move to the OxQL 2.1 packages with contract 2 (all five: OxQL.AspNetCore, OxQL.Model, OxQL.Core, OxQL.Mongo, OxQL.Studio). The base package compiles only against 2.1; a service that references an OxQL package itself moves to the same version, and the engine and this package are deployed together on every service that calls or is called. Explain (POST /OxQL/explain) is on by default, never executes a query and answers the request as it is bound (stages, aliases, types, result) in one call, rate limited per user and host; a host turns it off with OxQL:Explain:Enabled=false, which also closes POST internal/oxql/explain. A /OxQL/batch maxTimeMs now bounds the whole batch, not each query.

A request without the X-OxQL-Contract header is answered as the 1.1 engine in production answers it, by the engine's contract 1 legacy pipeline: every stored member under its stored name, lookups by collection name, the 1.1 cursor, count and refusals. It is the default (OxQL:Compat:Enabled, OxQL:Compat:Legacy:Enabled and OxQL:Compat:Legacy:Always are true), so reports and clients written against contract 1 keep working on an upgraded service without a change, and each such request is logged under OxQL.Compat.Legacy. A service owner should know: such a request may join any collection of the service's database by its name and reads of it the documents that carry the caller's organisation (as in production; OxQL:Compat:Legacy:AllowedLookupSources narrows it to named collections); the caller's organisation is now asked before any stage, so a group or a page written before the first match no longer reads other organisations' documents; a contract 1 request may run OxQL:Compat:Legacy:MaxTimeMs (ten minutes) in the database, not OxQL:Execution:MaxTimeMs. The legacy pipeline is temporary and removed once no caller needs it (the engine's LEGACY.md).

Under contract 2 a long and a decimal are JSON numbers in query results (rows, group keys and outputs, addon values), with every digit, as the REST API writes them; they were strings. A client typed against string changes its types; a reader that parses JSON numbers into doubles keeps 15 to 17 significant digits. Contract 1 answers are unchanged.

Publish Ox schema format 1.1: descriptions, constraints and deprecations, variants with their discriminator, onlyFor members and the name of a concrete base (baseVariant), reference cases and relation names (relation), members that are not stored (stored) and values stored otherwise than their kind says (storedAs), host-side reference declarations (OxSchemaOptionsBuilder) and the limits for continued stages, flatten depth and the report page. A 1.0 reader keeps reading the document.

Publish the model's own type member: a get-only string member of a polymorphic type that is a constant of each class (type: "driver") carries the value per variant (byVariant) and the distinct values (values). The query engine answers it in rows from the stored discriminator and filters it with eq, neq, in and nin; the entity lists its path in notSortable and no longer in notFilterable.

Every service's schema revision changes once when it takes this package, without a change to its model (the engine's published limits, the 1.1 format; and byVariant, values and notSortable where a service has a type member). A client that holds a schema document reloads it, and generated OxQL modules are regenerated.

Add POST internal/oxql/explain (internal api key) so another service checks the stages it continues here, as one batched call per round, at most OxQL:Explain:MaxConcurrentPerCaller (4) in flight per calling service (X-OxQL-Caller, sent by the RemoteQueryClient) and within the budget the origin has left, and pass internal batches to the engine as internal calls. The RemoteQueryClient reads an owner's shallow health before its first batch, names the routed API version and hands the engine the schema revision.

Store addon definitions in a collection per service (model_definition.addon_definition.{service}) with a unique index on organisation, entity and path among the rows not deleted; a write the index refuses is answered 409. The package creates the index at a process's first definition write; where the service's account may not create one, the writes go on, one warning is logged and the creation is asked for again an hour later. Read an entity's addon definitions under its current and every retired id in one query; a live row wins over a retired one.

Cache addon definitions per instance and serve them past their lifetime for at most ten lifetimes and never more than five minutes while one background read replaces them; requests that miss together share one read, and a request that waited for the read says it in its timing as database time. There is no invalidation across instances.
GET /schema is answered in the content coding the caller accepts.

The OxQL Studio console is served at {pathBase}/oxql (it answered only under a doubled path before) and only while OxQL:Studio:Enabled is true, which defaults to true in every environment but Production.
AuthorizeInternalApiKey runs before every other action filter, so a call without the key is answered 401 whatever its body holds.
